Definition: from G4130; replete, or covered over; by analogy, complete:--full.
BiblicalUsage: Pleres means full, replete, filled to the brim. The Word was made flesh, full of grace and truth, in John 1:14, and Jesus returned full of the Holy Ghost in Luke 4:1. Stephen was a man full of faith and of the Holy Ghost in Acts 6:5, and the church chose men full of the Holy Ghost and wisdom in Acts 6:3. After the feeding, twelve baskets full were taken up in Matthew 14:20.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe fullness is the mark of a life God has filled — grace, truth, faith, Spirit. My position is that an empty vessel makes the most noise, and a full one does the most good.
